class.name: VoxelGenerator
class.brief_description: Core voxel terrain generation engine with async support, LOD system, and terraforming capabilities.
class.description:
[b]VoxelGenerator[/b] is the core engine for procedural voxel terrain generation. It manages chunk-based terrain, asynchronous mesh generation, level-of-detail (LOD) systems, biome integration, terrain editing, and world boundary management (forcefields).
[b]Key Features:[/b] [ul] [li][b]Procedural Generation:[/b] Noise-based terrain with configurable amplitude, height, and detail[/li] [li][b]Async Generation:[/b] Non-blocking mesh generation via WorkerThreadPool for smooth gameplay[/li] [li][b]LOD System:[/b] Global and per-chunk distance-based LOD for performance optimization[/li] [li][b]Generation Modes:[/b] VOXELS_FIRST (full 3D) or HEIGHTMAP_FIRST (optimized 2D→3D)[/li] [li][b]Biome System:[/b] Multi-biome terrain with height, temperature, humidity blending[/li] [li][b]Feature Placement:[/b] Decorations, ores, trees, and other features via FeatureGenerator[/li] [li][b]Terraforming:[/b] Runtime terrain editing (dig/build spheres) with persistence[/li] [li][b]Forcefields:[/b] World boundary walls (6 directions) with collision and detection[/li] [li][b]Terrain Persistence:[/b] Save/load maps with terrain edits, background writer thread[/li] [li][b]Debug & Visualization:[/b] Noise visualization, voxel highlighting, LOD colors, chunk grid[/li] [/ul]
[b]Architecture Overview:[/b] The VoxelGenerator divides the world into chunks arranged in a 3D grid. Each chunk contains voxels (small cube volumes) whose type is determined by: 1. Procedural density evaluation (terrain_noise + detail_noise) 2. Biome assignment based on height/temperature/humidity 3. Features placed by FeatureGenerator (ores, trees, etc.) 4. Runtime terrain edits (dig/build operations)
Terrain is generated as mesh data via Marching Cubes isosurface extraction, either synchronously or asynchronously via WorkerThreadPool.
[b]Usage Workflow:[/b] [code] func _ready(): var generator = VoxelGenerator.new() add_child(generator)
# Configure world generator.set_world_size(Vector3i(16, 16, 16)) generator.set_chunk_size(8) generator.set_resolution(2)
# Configure noise var noise = NoiseGenerator.new() noise.set_period(64.0) noise.set_octaves(6) generator.set_terrain_noise(noise)
# Configure biome var biome_gen = BiomeGenerator.new() # ... setup biomes ... generator.set_biome_generator(biome_gen)
# Generate asynchronously with progress generator.generation_started.connect(_on_generation_started) generator.generation_progress.connect(_on_generation_progress) generator.generation_completed.connect(_on_generation_completed) generator.generate_async()
func _on_generation_completed(): print("Terrain generation complete!") [/code]
[b]Key Concepts:[/b] [ul] [li][b]Chunk:[/b] A cubic subdivision of terrain. Default 8×8×8 voxels. Chunks are independently generated and cached.[/li] [li][b]LOD (Level of Detail):[/b] Resolution reduction for distant chunks. LOD 0 = high detail, LOD 7 = lowest detail.[/li] [li][b]Density:[/b] Scalar value at each corner point. Negative = solid, positive = air. Marching Cubes extracts surface where density = cutoff.[/li] [li][b]Terrain Edits:[/b] Persistent modifications (dig/build) stored separately from procedural density.[/li] [li][b]Biome:[/b] Region with specific terrain characteristics (materials, noise scale, feature density).[/li] [li][b]Generation Mode:[/b] VOXELS_FIRST = full 3D density evaluation (flexible but slow). HEIGHTMAP_FIRST = 2D heightmap + surface band (fast).[/li] [/ul]
[b]Related Classes:[/b] [ul] [li][VoxelEngine] - High-level facade for lifecycle management[/li] [li][TerrainConfig] - Serializable terrain configuration presets[/li] [li][Chunk] - Individual terrain chunk representation[/li] [li][NoiseGenerator] - Noise configuration wrapper[/li] [li][BiomeGenerator] - Biome system with layering[/li] [li][FeatureGenerator] - Feature/decoration placement rules[/li] [/ul]

method.name: generate
method.description:
Generates the entire terrain synchronously (blocking call). All chunks are generated sequentially on the main thread.
[b]Behavior:[/b] [ol] [li]Builds density cache (samples all corner points)[/li] [li]Generates mesh for each chunk via Marching Cubes[/li] [li]Applies biome colors and features[/li] [li]Creates MeshInstance3D children for visible geometry[/li] [/ol]
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread. Blocks the thread until complete.
[b]Performance:[/b] For large worlds (16×16×16 or more), this can take several seconds. Consider [method generate_async] instead.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_world_size(Vector3i(8, 8, 8)) generator.generate() # Synchronous - waits until done print("Generation complete") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method generate_async], [method cancel_generation], [method is_generating]

method.name: generate_async
method.description:
Generates terrain asynchronously using WorkerThreadPool. Non-blocking - returns immediately while background threads do the work.
[b]Behavior:[/b] [ol] [li]Spawns worker threads via WorkerThreadPool[/li] [li]Worker threads generate chunk meshes in parallel[/li] [li]Main thread applies pending meshes via [method _process] (up to max_chunks_per_frame per frame)[/li] [li]Signals emitted during progression[/li] [/ol]
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from main thread. Worker threads handle mesh generation. Main thread applies results.
[b]Performance:[/b] Optimal for gameplay. Distributes work across frames to maintain smooth framerate.
[b]Signals Emitted:[/b] - [signal generation_started] - when generation begins - [signal generation_progress] - periodically during generation (every signal_every_n_chunks) - [signal generation_completed] - when all meshes are applied
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.generation_completed.connect(_on_gen_done) generator.generate_async()
func _on_gen_done(): print("Async generation complete") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method generate], [method cancel_generation], [method is_generating]

method.name: cancel_generation
method.description:
Cancels an in-progress async generation. Safe to call if no generation is running.
[b]Effect:[/b] - Stops worker threads from generating new chunks - Clears pending mesh queue - Emits [signal generation_cancelled]
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Note:[/b] Chunks already completed will remain rendered. Only future work is cancelled.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] if generator.is_generating(): generator.cancel_generation() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method generate_async], [method is_generating]

method.name: is_generating
method.description:
Returns true if generation is currently in progress.
[b]Return Value:[/b] True if async generation is active, false otherwise.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] if generator.is_generating(): print("Still generating...") else: print("Generation done") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method generate_async], [method cancel_generation]

method.name: set_generation_mode
method.description:
Sets the terrain generation mode: VOXELS_FIRST (0) or HEIGHTMAP_FIRST (1).
[b]Modes:[/b] [code]VOXELS_FIRST (0)[/code] - Full 3D density evaluation. Evaluate noise at every corner point. Supports complex overhangs and caves. slower. [code]HEIGHTMAP_FIRST (1)[/code] - Optimize for surface-focused terrain: Generate 2D heightmap, then evaluate density only in a surface band. Much faster for typical landscapes.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - 0 for VOXELS_FIRST, 1 for HEIGHTMAP_FIRST
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called when generation is not in progress.
[b]Performance Impact:[/b] HEIGHTMAP_FIRST is 2-4× faster for typical terrain but cannot generate caves above surface band.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_generation_mode(1) # Use fast heightmap mode generator.generate_async() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_generation_mode], [method set_surface_band], [method set_lod_level]

method.name: get_generation_mode
method.description:
Returns the current generation mode (0 = VOXELS_FIRST, 1 = HEIGHTMAP_FIRST).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_generation_mode]

method.name: set_lod_level
method.description:
Sets the global LOD (Level of Detail) level (0-7).
[b]LOD Levels:[/b] [code]0[/code] = Highest detail (all samples) [code]1[/code] = 1 sample per 2 corners (reduce resolution by ×2) [code]7[/code] = Lowest detail (sparse sampling)
Lower LOD = more detailed but slower. Higher LOD = faster but blockier.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Integer 0-7
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Can be set during generation. Takes effect on next chunk regeneration.
[b]Performance:[/b] Each LOD level reduces mesh generation time roughly by 2×. Useful for preview or distant chunks.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_lod_level(3) # Moderate detail generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_lod_level], [method set_enable_distance_lod], [method update_chunks_lod]

method.name: get_lod_level
method.description:
Returns the current global LOD level (0-7).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lod_level]

method.name: set_surface_band
method.description:
Sets the vertical band thickness around heightmap surface (HEIGHTMAP_FIRST mode only).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Height in world units (default 4.0). Only samples density within ±band around heightmap surface.
[b]Effect:[/b] Larger band = more voxels evaluated = slower but better for caves/overhangs. Smaller band = faster but may miss underground features.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Can be set anytime. Takes effect on next chunk regeneration.
[b]Note:[/b] Only applies in HEIGHTMAP_FIRST mode. Ignored in VOXELS_FIRST.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_generation_mode(1) # HEIGHTMAP_FIRST generator.set_surface_band(6.0) # Larger band for more detail [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_surface_band], [method set_generation_mode]

method.name: get_surface_band
method.description:
Returns the current surface band thickness.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_surface_band]

method.name: set_enable_distance_lod
method.description:
Enables or disables per-chunk distance-based LOD.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - true to enable distance LOD, false to use global LOD for all chunks
[b]Behavior:[/b] When enabled, each chunk's LOD is computed based on its distance from [member lod_reference_position]. Chunks closer to the reference use finer LOD, distant chunks use coarser LOD.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Can be changed anytime. Call [method update_chunks_lod] to recompute.
[b]Performance:[/b] Significantly improves framerate for large worlds (16×16×16+) by prioritizing detail near player/camera.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_enable_distance_lod(true) generator.set_lod_reference_position(player.get_global_position()) generator.update_chunks_lod() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_enable_distance_lod], [method set_lod_reference_position], [method set_lod_distances], [method update_chunks_lod]

method.name: get_enable_distance_lod
method.description:
Returns whether distance-based LOD is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_enable_distance_lod]

method.name: set_lod_reference_position
method.description:
Sets the reference position for distance-based LOD calculations (typically player/camera position).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - World position to measure distance from
[b]Effect:[/b] Used with [method update_chunks_lod] to compute per-chunk LOD based on distance. Call this in _process() with player position for dynamic LOD.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] func _process(delta): if generator.get_enable_distance_lod(): generator.set_lod_reference_position(player.get_global_position()) if generator.update_chunks_lod() > 0: # Some chunks changed LOD, they'll regenerate pass [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_lod_reference_position], [method set_lod_distances], [method update_chunks_lod]

method.name: get_lod_reference_position
method.description:
Returns the current LOD reference position.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lod_reference_position]

method.name: set_lod_distances
method.description:
Sets the distance thresholds for LOD levels (0-7).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Array of 8 float values. value[0] = max distance for LOD 0, value[1] = max distance for LOD 1, etc.
[b]Behavior:[/b] - If chunk distance ≤ value[0]: LOD 0 (high detail) - If chunk distance ≤ value[1]: LOD 1 - ... and so on ... - If chunk distance > value[7]: LOD 7 (lowest detail)
[b]Default Formula:[/b] By default, distances follow: value[n] = chunk_size × (2 ^ n) × lod_distance_multiplier
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var distances = PackedFloat64Array([32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096]) generator.set_lod_distances(distances) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_lod_distances], [method reset_lod_distances_to_default], [method update_chunks_lod]

method.name: get_lod_distances
method.description:
Returns the current LOD distance thresholds (array of 8 values).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lod_distances]

method.name: reset_lod_distances_to_default
method.description:
Resets LOD distance thresholds to algorithmically calculated defaults based on chunk_size.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_lod_distances([...custom values...]) # ... later ... generator.reset_lod_distances_to_default() # Back to defaults [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lod_distances], [method get_lod_distances]

method.name: update_chunks_lod
method.description:
Updates per-chunk LOD levels based on distance from reference position. Marks chunks that changed LOD as dirty.
[b]Return Value:[/b] Number of chunks that changed LOD and were marked dirty (need regeneration).
[b]Behavior:[/b] - Computes distance from each chunk center to [member lod_reference_position] - Assigns LOD level based on [member lod_distances] - Marks changed chunks as dirty - Returns count of changed chunks
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call frequently (e.g., per frame).
[b]Performance:[/b] O(num_chunks) calculation. Cheap unless many chunks change LOD.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var changed = generator.update_chunks_lod() if changed > 0: print("Updated LOD for ", changed, " chunks") generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_lod_reference_position], [method set_lod_distances], [method mark_chunk_dirty]

method.name: calculate_chunk_lod
method.description:
Calculates the LOD level for a specific chunk based on distance (if distance LOD enabled).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]chunk_index[/code] - Linear chunk index (0 to num_chunks - 1)
[b]Return Value:[/b] LOD level (0-7). Returns global lod_level if distance LOD disabled.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var lod = generator.calculate_chunk_lod(5) print("Chunk 5 LOD: ", lod) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_enable_distance_lod], [method set_lod_level]

method.name: set_terrain_noise
method.description:
Sets the noise generator for base terrain height generation.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_noise[/code] - A [NoiseGenerator] resource configured with desired noise parameters.
[b]Effect:[/b] This noise determines the primary shape of terrain (mountains, valleys, plains). Call [method regenerate_dirty_chunks] or regenerate to apply changes.
[b]Default:[/b] Must be explicitly set before generation. No default noise is configured.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var noise = NoiseGenerator.new() noise.set_period(64.0) noise.set_octaves(6) generator.set_terrain_noise(noise) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_terrain_noise], [method set_detail_noise], [method NoiseGenerator]

method.name: get_terrain_noise
method.description:
Returns the currently set terrain noise generator.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_terrain_noise]

method.name: set_detail_noise
method.description:
Sets the noise generator for detail (rocky) features.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_noise[/code] - A [NoiseGenerator] resource for 3D rocky detail.
[b]Effect:[/b] Applied with [member rock_influence] factor to add surface variation and caves. Lower frequencies create rough surfaces, higher frequencies create fine detail.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var detail_noise = NoiseGenerator.new() detail_noise.set_period(16.0) detail_noise.set_octaves(4) generator.set_detail_noise(detail_noise) generator.set_rock_influence(0.4) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_detail_noise], [method set_terrain_noise], [method set_rock_influence]

method.name: get_detail_noise
method.description:
Returns the currently set detail noise generator.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_detail_noise]

method.name: set_rock_influence
method.description:
Sets the strength of detail noise influence (0.0-1.0).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Blending factor. 0.0 = no detail, 1.0 = full detail applied. Default 0.3.
[b]Effect:[/b] Multiplier for how much the detail_noise affects terrain. Higher values create more jagged, cave-filled terrain.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_rock_influence(0.2) # Subtle surface texture generator.set_rock_influence(0.7) # Very rocky, many caves [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_rock_influence], [method set_detail_noise]

method.name: get_rock_influence
method.description:
Returns the current rock influence factor (0.0-1.0).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_rock_influence]

method.name: set_terrain_height
method.description:
Sets the base terrain height (center height of terrain in world units).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Height offset. Default 4.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] This is the Y-coordinate around which terrain oscillates. Higher values shift terrain up. Used with [member terrain_amplitude] to define elevation range.
[b]Range:[/b] terrain_min = terrain_height - terrain_amplitude terrain_max = terrain_height + terrain_amplitude
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_terrain_height(10.0) # Center at Y=10 generator.set_terrain_amplitude(15.0) # Range: Y=-5 to Y=25 [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_terrain_height], [method set_terrain_amplitude]

method.name: get_terrain_height
method.description:
Returns the current base terrain height.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_terrain_height]

method.name: set_terrain_amplitude
method.description:
Sets the height variation range (±amplitude from base height).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Range in world units. Default 8.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] Combined with [member terrain_height]. Larger amplitudes create more dramatic height variation.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Flat terrain generator.set_terrain_amplitude(1.0)
# Mountainous terrain generator.set_terrain_amplitude(20.0) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_terrain_amplitude], [method set_terrain_height]

method.name: get_terrain_amplitude
method.description:
Returns the current terrain amplitude.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_terrain_amplitude]

method.name: set_biome_generator
method.description:
Sets the biome generator that determines voxel types based on height/temperature/humidity.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_generator[/code] - A [BiomeGenerator] resource with configured biomes.
[b]Effect:[/b] The biome generator is consulted during chunk generation to assign voxel types (sand, stone, grass, etc.) based on position and biome characteristics. Essential for terrain variety.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var biome_gen = BiomeGenerator.new() # Configure biomes... biome_gen.add_biome("grass", 2.0, 8.0, ...) biome_gen.add_biome("desert", -1.0, 2.0, ...) generator.set_biome_generator(biome_gen) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_biome_generator], [method set_feature_generator], [method BiomeGenerator]

method.name: get_biome_generator
method.description:
Returns the currently set biome generator.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_biome_generator]

method.name: set_feature_generator
method.description:
Sets the feature generator that places decorations, ores, trees, etc.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_generator[/code] - A [FeatureGenerator] resource with configured placement rules.
[b]Effect:[/b] After biome terrain is generated, features are placed according to rules (probability, biome filters, height ranges, clustering).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var feature_gen = FeatureGenerator.new() feature_gen.add_ore_rule(VOXEL_IRON, 0.3, 2, 50) # Iron ore feature_gen.add_tree_rule(0.1, [BIOME_FOREST], 5, 20) # Trees in forests generator.set_feature_generator(feature_gen) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_feature_generator], [method set_biome_generator], [method FeatureGenerator]

method.name: get_feature_generator
method.description:
Returns the currently set feature generator.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_feature_generator]

method.name: set_resolution
method.description:
Sets the sampling resolution (samples per voxel edge).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Integer ≥ 1. Default 1. Higher = more detail but slower.
[b]Effect:[/b] Resolution 1 = one sample per voxel corner (standard marching cubes). Resolution 2 = four samples per edge (more accurate surface). Resolution 3+ = even finer detail at significant cost.
[b]Performance:[/b] Each increment roughly 2× slower due to more density evaluations.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_resolution(1) # Fast, blocky generator.set_resolution(3) # Slow, very smooth [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_resolution], [method set_lod_level]

method.name: get_resolution
method.description:
Returns the current sampling resolution.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_resolution]

method.name: set_cutoff
method.description:
Sets the density cutoff threshold for marching cubes (where surface is extracted).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Threshold density. Default 0.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] Marching cubes generates surface where density crosses this threshold. Negative density = solid, positive = air. Raising cutoff (negative direction) creates more solid terrain; lowering it creates more air.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_cutoff(-0.5) # More solid terrain generator.set_cutoff(0.0) # Balanced generator.set_cutoff(0.5) # More hollow/air [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_cutoff]

method.name: get_cutoff
method.description:
Returns the current density cutoff threshold.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_cutoff]

method.name: set_seeder
method.description:
Sets the random seed for noise generation and feature placement.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Seed integer (default 1240). Same seed produces identical terrain.
[b]Effect:[/b] Used by noise generators and randomization functions. Changing seed changes terrain while keeping structure similar.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_seeder(42) # Deterministic terrain generator.set_randomizer(false) generator.generate()
# Generate again - identical result generator.generate() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_seeder], [method set_randomizer]

method.name: get_seeder
method.description:
Returns the current random seed.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_seeder]

method.name: set_randomizer
method.description:
Enables/disables random seed variation.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - true to randomize seed each generation, false to use fixed [member seeder].
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, seed is randomized before each generate() call, creating different terrain. When disabled, same seed used = same terrain (unless other parameters change).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_randomizer(true) generator.generate() # Random terrain #1 generator.generate() # Random terrain #2 (different) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_randomizer], [method set_seeder]

method.name: get_randomizer
method.description:
Returns whether random seed variation is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_randomizer]

method.name: set_world_size
method.description:
Sets the world grid dimensions (in chunks).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Grid size. E.g., Vector3i(16, 16, 16) = 16×16×16 chunks.
[b]Effect:[/b] Total voxels = world_size × chunk_size. For example, 16 chunks × 8 voxels = 128 voxel units per dimension.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Cannot be changed after first generation (world_size_finalized flag prevents drift). Call [method reset] to allow new size.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_world_size(Vector3i(8, 8, 8)) # 512 chunks total generator.set_chunk_size(8) generator.generate() # Now world_size_finalized = true, can't change size [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_world_size], [method set_chunk_size], [method reset]

method.name: get_world_size
method.description:
Returns the current world grid dimensions (in chunks).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_world_size]

method.name: set_chunk_size
method.description:
Sets the chunk dimensions (voxels per chunk edge).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Size. Default 8. Common values: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Must be within Constants::MIN_CHUNK_SIZE to Constants::MAX_CHUNK_SIZE.
[b]Effect:[/b] - Chunk 8×8×8 = 512 voxels per chunk - Chunk 16×16×16 = 4096 voxels per chunk - Larger chunks = fewer total chunks but slower individual chunk generation.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Should be set before first generation.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_chunk_size(8) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_chunk_size], [method set_world_size]

method.name: get_chunk_size
method.description:
Returns the current chunk size (voxels per edge).
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_chunk_size]

method.name: set_show_centers
method.description:
Enables debug visualization of chunk centers.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, small cubes are drawn at the center of each chunk for visual debugging.
[b]Performance:[/b] Minimal overhead. Enable only for debugging.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_show_centers], [method set_show_voxel_grid], [method set_show_chunk_grid], [method set_show_lod_colors]

method.name: get_show_centers
method.description:
Returns whether chunk center visualization is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_show_centers]

method.name: set_show_voxel_grid
method.description:
Enables debug visualization of voxel grid lines.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, a 3D grid is rendered showing voxel boundaries.
[b]Performance:[/b] Can be slow for large worlds. Use only for small debug sessions.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_show_voxel_grid], [method set_show_chunk_grid], [method set_show_centers]

method.name: get_show_voxel_grid
method.description:
Returns whether voxel grid visualization is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_show_voxel_grid]

method.name: set_show_chunk_grid
method.description:
Enables debug visualization of chunk grid boundaries.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, wireframe boxes are drawn around each chunk.
[b]Performance:[/b] Lightweight visualization. Good for spatial debugging without overwhelming detail.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_show_chunk_grid], [method set_show_voxel_grid], [method set_show_centers]

method.name: get_show_chunk_grid
method.description:
Returns whether chunk grid visualization is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_show_chunk_grid]

method.name: set_vertex_limit
method.description:
Enables/disables vertex count limits per chunk.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - true to cap vertices, false for unlimited.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, mesh generation stops if vertex limit reached (prevents degenerate meshes). For most cases, leave enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_vertex_limit]

method.name: get_vertex_limit
method.description:
Returns whether vertex limiting is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_vertex_limit]

method.name: set_max_chunks_per_frame
method.description:
Sets the maximum number of chunks to apply mesh per frame during async generation (1-32).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Chunk count. Default 4.
[b]Effect:[/b] Higher = faster streaming but more frame stuttering. Lower = smoother but slower streaming. Tune based on frame budget and hardware.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_max_chunks_per_frame(2) # Conservative, very smooth generator.set_max_chunks_per_frame(8) # Aggressive, faster generation [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_max_chunks_per_frame], [method set_signal_every_n_chunks]

method.name: get_max_chunks_per_frame
method.description:
Returns the current max chunks per frame setting.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_max_chunks_per_frame]

method.name: set_signal_every_n_chunks
method.description:
Sets the signal emission frequency during async generation (1-64).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - Signal every N chunks completed. Default 8.
[b]Effect:[/b] Lower = more frequent progress updates (more signals, finer granularity). Higher = fewer signals (less overhead, coarser updates).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_signal_every_n_chunks(1) # Signal per chunk generator.set_signal_every_n_chunks(16) # Signal every 16 chunks [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_signal_every_n_chunks], [signal generation_progress]

method.name: get_signal_every_n_chunks
method.description:
Returns the current signal frequency setting.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_signal_every_n_chunks]

method.name: mark_chunk_dirty
method.description:
Marks a specific chunk as needing regeneration.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]chunk_coord[/code] - 3D grid coordinate (e.g., Vector3i(0, 0, 0) for first chunk).
[b]Effect:[/b] Sets dirty flag. Call [method regenerate_dirty_chunks] to update.
[b]Use Case:[/b] After calling [method modify_terrain] or changing biome/feature settings locally, mark affected chunks dirty.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.modify_terrain(Vector3(50, 10, 50), 5.0, -1.0) # Dig sphere generator.mark_chunk_dirty(Vector3i(6, 1, 6)) # Mark affected chunk generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method is_chunk_dirty], [method mark_all_chunks_dirty], [method regenerate_dirty_chunks]

method.name: mark_all_chunks_dirty
method.description:
Marks all chunks as needing regeneration.
[b]Effect:[/b] Sets dirty flag on every chunk. Call [method regenerate_dirty_chunks] to update all.
[b]Use Case:[/b] After global changes (changing noise, terrain height, etc.) to force complete regeneration.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_terrain_height(15.0) generator.mark_all_chunks_dirty() generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method mark_chunk_dirty], [method regenerate_dirty_chunks]

method.name: is_chunk_dirty
method.description:
Checks if a chunk is marked as dirty (needs regeneration).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]chunk_coord[/code] - 3D grid coordinate.
[b]Return Value:[/b] true if chunk is dirty, false otherwise.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] if generator.is_chunk_dirty(Vector3i(5, 0, 5)): print("Chunk needs regeneration") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method mark_chunk_dirty], [method regenerate_dirty_chunks]

method.name: regenerate_dirty_chunks
method.description:
Regenerates all chunks marked as dirty (incremental update).
[b]Behavior:[/b] Triggers async generation for only dirt chunks. Much faster than full [method generate].
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.modify_terrain(center, radius, delta) generator.mark_chunk_dirty(chunk_coord) generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method mark_chunk_dirty], [method mark_all_chunks_dirty], [method generate_async]

method.name: invalidate_density_region
method.description:
Invalidates cached density values in a region (call after terrain edits).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]min_voxel[/code], [code]max_voxel[/code] - Bounding box of affected area.
[b]Effect:[/b] Clears density cache for the region so next access recomputes from edits. Important for terraforming to avoid stale cache.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.modify_terrain(center, radius, delta) generator.invalidate_density_region(center - radius, center + radius) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method modify_terrain], [method regenerate_dirty_chunks]

method.name: modify_terrain
method.description:
Modifies terrain in a spherical region with smooth falloff.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]center[/code] - World position of edit sphere center. [code]radius[/code] - Radius of effect (world units). [code]delta[/code] - Density change. Negative = dig (remove terrain), positive = build (add terrain). Typical range: ±1.0.
[b]Effect:[/b] Applies smooth falloff from center outward. Density at center = delta, fades to 0 at radius boundary. Changes are persistent across regenerations.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime. Mutations are thread-safe via internal mutex.
[b]Performance:[/b] Each call modifies affected voxels. Multiple edits can be accumulated efficiently.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Dig a hole generator.modify_terrain(Vector3(50, 20, 50), 10.0, -2.0)
# Build terrain generator.modify_terrain(Vector3(60, 20, 60), 5.0, 1.5)
# Regenerate to see changes generator.mark_all_chunks_dirty() generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method dig_sphere], [method build_sphere], [method clear_terrain_edits], [method invalidate_density_region]

method.name: dig_sphere
method.description:
Convenience method to dig (remove) terrain in a sphere.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]center[/code] - Sphere center. [code]radius[/code] - Sphere radius. [code]strength[/code] - Dig intensity (default 1.0). Higher = deeper excavation.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]modify_terrain(center, radius, -strength)[/code]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.dig_sphere(player_pos, 5.0, 1.5) # Dig where player stands [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method build_sphere], [method modify_terrain]

method.name: build_sphere
method.description:
Convenience method to build (add) terrain in a sphere.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]center[/code] - Sphere center. [code]radius[/code] - Sphere radius. [code]strength[/code] - Build intensity (default 1.0). Higher = more terrain added.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]modify_terrain(center, radius, +strength)[/code]
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.build_sphere(world_pos, 3.0, 1.0) # Build wall [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method dig_sphere], [method modify_terrain]

method.name: clear_terrain_edits
method.description:
Clears all terrain edits, resetting to procedurally generated terrain.
[b]Effect:[/b] Removes all dig/build modifications. Terrain reverts to noise-based generation.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call anytime.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Make edits generator.dig_sphere(pos1, 10.0, 1.0) generator.build_sphere(pos2, 5.0, 1.0)
# Reset generator.clear_terrain_edits() generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method modify_terrain], [method get_terrain_edit_count]

method.name: get_terrain_edit_count
method.description:
Returns the number of stored terrain edits (voxels modified by dig/build).
[b]Return Value:[/b] Number of edited voxels.
[b]Use Case:[/b] Check if terrain has unsaved edits or gauge edit complexity.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] if generator.get_terrain_edit_count() > 0: print("Unsaved edits present") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method clear_terrain_edits], [method get_terrain_edits_data]

method.name: get_terrain_edits_data
method.description:
Serializes terrain edits to a packed array for saving.
[b]Return Value:[/b] Array of floats encoding all edits: [x, y, z, delta, x, y, z, delta, ...].
[b]Use Case:[/b] Call before save_map() or for manual persistence.
[b]Format:[/b] Array is length = 4 × num_edits. Each edit is 4 floats: (x, y, z, delta).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var edits_data = generator.get_terrain_edits_data() save_file.store_var(edits_data) # Save [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_terrain_edits_data], [method save_map]

method.name: set_terrain_edits_data
method.description:
Deserializes terrain edits from a packed array.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]data[/code] - Array from [method get_terrain_edits_data].
[b]Effect:[/b] Restores edits from saved format. Replaces any existing edits.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var edits_data = save_file.get_var() # Load generator.set_terrain_edits_data(edits_data) generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_terrain_edits_data], [method load_map]

method.name: set_forcefield_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables the forcefield (world boundary system).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]enabled[/code] - true to enable, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, creates 6 boundary walls (north, south, east, west, top, bottom) around the world. Players are contained within. When disabled, walls are removed.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread. Modifies scene graph.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_enabled(true) generator.set_forcefield_height(100.0) generator.create_forcefield_nodes() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_enabled], [method set_forcefield_height], [method set_forcefield_wall_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the forcefield is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_height
method.description:
Sets the height of forcefield walls.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]h[/code] - Height in world units (default 300.0).
[b]Effect:[/b] Extends walls vertically. Taller walls contain taller objects.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_height(500.0) # Very tall barrier [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_height], [method set_forcefield_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_height
method.description:
Returns the current forcefield height.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_height]

method.name: set_forcefield_collision_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables collision on forcefield walls.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]enabled[/code] - true for solid walls, false for invisible barriers.
[b]Effect:[/b] When true, walls have physics and block movement. When false, walls are visual only.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_collision_enabled(true) # Players can't pass [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_collision_enabled], [method set_forcefield_detection_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_collision_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether collision is enabled on forcefields.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_collision_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_detection_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables detection zones (Area3D) on forcefield walls.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]enabled[/code] - true to detect bodies entering walls, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, forcefield provides [signal forcefield_body_entered], [signal forcefield_body_exited] signals. Walls can fade visibility when player is inside.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_detection_enabled(true) generator.forcefield_body_entered.connect(_on_forcefield_entered) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_detection_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_detection_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether detection zones are enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_detection_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_buffer
method.description:
Sets the inward buffer distance from world boundary to wall placement.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]buf[/code] - Distance in voxel units (default 0.5). Walls are inset by this amount.
[b]Effect:[/b] Prevents walls from being exactly at boundary edge, giving them some clearance.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_buffer(2.0) # Walls inset 2 voxels [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_buffer], [method set_forcefield_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_buffer
method.description:
Returns the current forcefield buffer distance.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_buffer]

method.name: set_forcefield_shader_material
method.description:
Sets a custom shader material for forcefield walls.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]material[/code] - A [ShaderMaterial] resource for rendering walls.
[b]Effect:[/b] Applied to all forcefield wall meshes. Allows custom visuals (glow, fade, animation, etc.).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var mat = ShaderMaterial.new() mat.shader = load("res://shaders/forcefield.gdshader") generator.set_forcefield_shader_material(mat) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_shader_material], [method set_forcefield_shader_param]

method.name: get_forcefield_shader_material
method.description:
Returns the current forcefield shader material.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_shader_material]

method.name: set_forcefield_wall_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables a specific forcefield wall by index.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]wall_index[/code] - 0=North, 1=South, 2=East, 3=West, 4=Top, 5=Bottom. [code]enabled[/code] - true to enable, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] Individual walls can be toggled independently. Useful for portals or gaps.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] # Allow north exit generator.set_forcefield_wall_enabled(0, false) # Disable north [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_forcefield_wall_enabled], [method set_forcefield_north_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_wall_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether a specific wall is enabled.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]wall_index[/code] - 0=North, 1=South, 2=East, 3=West, 4=Top, 5=Bottom.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_wall_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_north_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the north wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(0, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_south_enabled], [method set_forcefield_east_enabled], [method set_forcefield_west_enabled], [method set_forcefield_top_enabled], [method set_forcefield_bottom_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_north_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the north wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_north_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_south_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the south wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(1, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_north_enabled], [method set_forcefield_east_enabled], [method set_forcefield_west_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_south_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the south wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_south_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_east_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the east wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(2, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_north_enabled], [method set_forcefield_west_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_east_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the east wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_east_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_west_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the west wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(3, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_north_enabled], [method set_forcefield_east_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_west_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the west wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_west_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_top_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the top (ceiling) wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(4, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_bottom_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_top_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the top wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_top_enabled]

method.name: set_forcefield_bottom_enabled
method.description:
Convenience method to enable/disable the bottom (floor) wall.
[b]Equivalent To:[/b] [code]set_forcefield_wall_enabled(5, enabled)[/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_top_enabled]

method.name: get_forcefield_bottom_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether the bottom wall is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_forcefield_bottom_enabled]

method.name: create_forcefield_nodes
method.description:
Creates the forcefield wall scene nodes (MeshInstance3D, StaticBody3D, CollisionShape3D, Area3D).
[b]Effect:[/b] Builds and adds forcefield geometry to the scene tree as children of this generator node.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_enabled(true) generator.set_forcefield_height(300.0) generator.create_forcefield_nodes() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method update_forcefield_nodes], [method remove_forcefield_nodes]

method.name: update_forcefield_nodes
method.description:
Updates forcefield wall geometry (e.g., after changing height or buffer).
[b]Effect:[/b] Rebuilds wall meshes and collision shapes with current parameters.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_height(500.0) generator.update_forcefield_nodes() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method create_forcefield_nodes], [method remove_forcefield_nodes]

method.name: remove_forcefield_nodes
method.description:
Removes the forcefield wall nodes from the scene tree.
[b]Effect:[/b] Cleans up all forcefield geometry.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_forcefield_enabled(false) generator.remove_forcefield_nodes() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method create_forcefield_nodes]

method.name: save_map
method.description:
Saves the terrain map (chunks and edits) to disk.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]dir[/code] - Base directory (e.g., "user://maps", "res://maps"). [code]map_name[/code] - Subdirectory name for this map within base directory.
[b]Structure:[/b] Files saved to: [code]{dir}/{map_name}/*[/code] - Chunk meshes stored as binary .chunk files - Terrain edits stored in metadata
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call. Background writer thread handles I/O.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.save_map("user://maps", "my_world") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method load_map], [method start_background_writer], [method stop_background_writer]

method.name: load_map
method.description:
Loads a previously saved terrain map.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]dir[/code] - Base directory path. [code]map_name[/code] - Map subdirectory name. [code]strict_match[/code] - If true, map must match current world size. If false, load what's available.
[b]Effect:[/b] Loads chunk meshes and terrain edits, reconstructing previous state.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.load_map("user://maps", "my_world", true) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method save_map]

method.name: set_debug_mode
method.description:
Enables/disables debug output logging.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_enabled[/code] - true to enable, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, generator emits debug messages to console. Output level controlled by [method set_debug_verbosity].
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_debug_mode(true) generator.set_debug_verbosity(2) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_debug_mode], [method set_debug_verbosity]

method.name: get_debug_mode
method.description:
Returns whether debug mode is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_debug_mode]

method.name: set_visualize_noise_values
method.description:
Enables/disables noise field visualization.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_enabled[/code] - true to visualize, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, a 2D slice of noise values is rendered for debugging noise configuration.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_visualize_noise_values(true) generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_visualize_noise_values], [method debug_draw_noise_slice]

method.name: get_visualize_noise_values
method.description:
Returns whether noise visualization is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_visualize_noise_values]

method.name: set_debug_verbosity
method.description:
Sets the debug output verbosity level (0-3).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]p_level[/code] - 0=silent, 1=errors, 2=info, 3=verbose.
[b]Effect:[/b] Higher levels produce more console output. Only active if [method set_debug_mode] enabled.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_debug_mode(true) generator.set_debug_verbosity(3) # Maximum verbosity [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_debug_verbosity], [method set_debug_mode]

method.name: get_debug_verbosity
method.description:
Returns the current debug verbosity level.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_debug_verbosity]

method.name: set_debug_dump_chunk_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables per-chunk density sampling dump (instrumentation).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]enabled[/code] - true to enable, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, designated chunk outputs detailed density samples to console for analysis. Used to verify density calculations.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_debug_dump_chunk_enabled(true) generator.set_debug_dump_chunk_coord(Vector3i(1, 0, 0)) generator.generate() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_debug_dump_chunk_enabled], [method set_debug_dump_chunk_coord], [method dump_chunk_density_samples]

method.name: get_debug_dump_chunk_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether chunk density dump is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_debug_dump_chunk_enabled]

method.name: set_debug_dump_chunk_coord
method.description:
Sets which chunk to sample density for dumping.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]coord[/code] - 3D chunk coordinate (e.g., Vector3i(1, 0, 0)).
[b]Effect:[/b] When chunk dump is enabled, this chunk's density values are logged.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_debug_dump_chunk_coord(Vector3i(5, 2, 5)) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_debug_dump_chunk_coord], [method dump_chunk_density_samples]

method.name: get_debug_dump_chunk_coord
method.description:
Returns the chunk coordinate set for density dump.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_debug_dump_chunk_coord]

method.name: dump_chunk_density_samples
method.description:
Manually triggers density sampling dump for a chunk.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]chunk_index[/code] - Linear chunk index.
[b]Effect:[/b] Outputs detailed density values at all corner points of the chunk to console.
[b]Use Case:[/b] Debugging terrain generation issues or verifying noise output.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.dump_chunk_density_samples(5) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_debug_dump_chunk_enabled]

method.name: set_voxel_highlight_enabled
method.description:
Enables/disables voxel highlighting (debug visualization).
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]enabled[/code] - true to enable, false to disable.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, voxel at [member highlight_position] is highlighted with [member highlight_color].
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_voxel_highlight_enabled(true) generator.set_highlight_position(player.get_position()) generator.set_highlight_color(Color.GREEN) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_voxel_highlight_enabled], [method set_highlight_position], [method set_highlight_color]

method.name: get_voxel_highlight_enabled
method.description:
Returns whether voxel highlighting is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_voxel_highlight_enabled]

method.name: set_highlight_position
method.description:
Sets the world position to highlight.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]position[/code] - World position for highlight.
[b]Effect:[/b] Used with [method set_voxel_highlight_enabled]. Nearest voxel to this position is highlighted.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] func _process(_delta): generator.set_highlight_position(player.get_position()) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_highlight_position], [method set_voxel_highlight_enabled]

method.name: get_highlight_position
method.description:
Returns the current highlight position.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_highlight_position]

method.name: set_highlight_color
method.description:
Sets the color of highlighted voxels.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]color[/code] - Highlight color (default bright yellow).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_highlight_color(Color.RED) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_highlight_color]

method.name: get_highlight_color
method.description:
Returns the current highlight color.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_highlight_color]

method.name: clear_highlight
method.description:
Clears all highlight visualization.
[b]Effect:[/b] Disables highlighting without changing enable flag.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_voxel_highlight_enabled]

method.name: set_show_lod_colors
method.description:
Enables/disables LOD color visualization.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - true to color chunks by LOD, false for normal colors.
[b]Effect:[/b] When enabled, chunks are colored from green (LOD 0) to red (LOD 7) for visual validation of LOD assignment.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_enable_distance_lod(true) generator.set_show_lod_colors(true) generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_show_lod_colors], [method set_enable_distance_lod]

method.name: get_show_lod_colors
method.description:
Returns whether LOD color visualization is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_show_lod_colors]

method.name: set_use_textures
method.description:
Toggles between textured and vertex-color rendering.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - true for textured, false for vertex colors.
[b]Effect:[/b] When true, terrain uses texture maps. When false, uses per-vertex colors (useful for debug/biome visualization).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.set_use_textures(false) # Show biome colors generator.regenerate_dirty_chunks() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_use_textures], [method set_terrain_material]

method.name: get_use_textures
method.description:
Returns whether textured rendering is enabled.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_use_textures]

method.name: set_terrain_material
method.description:
Sets the material applied to all terrain chunks.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]value[/code] - A [Material] (StandardMaterial3D, ShaderMaterial, etc.).
[b]Effect:[/b] Applied to all chunk MeshInstance3D nodes. Useful for consistent styling, lighting, or special effects.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var mat = StandardMaterial3D.new() mat.albedo_color = Color.GREEN generator.set_terrain_material(mat) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_terrain_material], [method set_use_textures]

method.name: get_terrain_material
method.description:
Returns the current terrain material.
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_terrain_material]

method.name: sample_density_at
method.description:
Samples the density at a world position.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]world_pos[/code] - World position to sample.
[b]Return Value:[/b] Density value (negative = solid, positive = air, zero = surface).
[b]Use Case:[/b] Querying density for gameplay logic (digging, building, etc.).
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread (uses read-write lock on cache).
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var density = generator.sample_density_at(player.position) if density < 0: print("Player is underground") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_voxel_at]

method.name: get_voxel_at
method.description:
Gets the voxel type at integer voxel coordinates.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]voxel_pos[/code] - Integer voxel position (e.g., Vector3i(100, 50, 100)).
[b]Return Value:[/b] Voxel type ID (0 = AIR, 1+ = specific voxel type like STONE, DIRT, etc.).
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var voxel_type = generator.get_voxel_at(Vector3i(100, 50, 100)) if voxel_type == VOXEL_STONE: print("Stone found") [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method sample_density_at]

method.name: debug_print_state
method.description:
Prints generator state information to console (debug).
[b]Effect:[/b] Outputs world size, chunk size, resolution, LOD mode, noise generators, timings, etc.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.debug_print_state() [/code]

method.name: debug_draw_noise_slice
method.description:
Draws a debug visualization of noise values at a specific Y level.
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]y_level[/code] - Y world coordinate to slice at.
[b]Effect:[/b] Creates an ImmediateMesh visualization showing the noise profile at that height level.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.debug_draw_noise_slice(10.0) # Slice at Y=10 [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_visualize_noise_values]

method.name: reset
method.description:
Resets the generator to initial state.
[b]Effect:[/b] Clears density cache, terrain edits, chunks, and resets flags. Allows changing world_size again.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from main thread when generation is not in progress.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] generator.reset() generator.set_world_size(Vector3i(32, 32, 32)) generator.generate() [/code]
